subject: biology
title: The Menstrual Cycle
welcome_lead: Learn the simple monthly cycle that prepares the body for possible pregnancy.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on the menstrual cycle at a simple level.
final_note: You can now describe the basic stages of the menstrual cycle.

concepts.def: Release of an egg from the ovary.
Loss of uterus lining and a little blood.
Organ that stores and releases eggs.

walkthroughs.body_html: The menstrual cycle lasts about 28 days. It is controlled by hormones from the brain and ovaries.
Around day 14, an egg is released from an ovary. If a sperm meets it, fertilisation may happen and pregnancy can start.
If no fertilisation happens, the lining of the uterus breaks down. This is called a period and lasts a few days at the start of the cycle.

mcqs.q: Why is the secondary immune response to a pathogen faster and stronger than the primary?
options: The body produces a different, more powerful antibody during the secondary response.
The pathogen becomes weaker after the primary exposure, so the body has an easier job.
Memory cells generated during the primary response can rapidly proliferate and produce large amounts of specific antibody on re-exposure.
The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.

mcqs.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right?
options: The left ventricle is thicker because it handles oxygenated blood, which is harder to pump.
Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
It must pump blood at high pressure around the whole body; the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.
